text: The Hickinbottom Award, also known as the Hickinbottom Fellowship, is given annually by the Royal Society of Chemistry to an early career scientist for outstanding contributions in organic chemistry. The recipient receives a monetary prize and is required to complete a lecture tour across the UK. The award is selected by the awards committee of the Royal Society of Chemistry's organic division. It was established in 1979 through a bequest from Wilfred Hickinbottom, who was recognized for his support of high standards in experimental chemistry. A portion of the monetary award is the Briggs scholarship, which was funded by a bequest from Lady Alice Lilian Thorpe, the daughter of William Briggs. The award was first presented in 1981 to Steven Ley and Jeremy Sanders. Subsequent recipients are listed in the records.
